rungDetail.rung2: REACHED AND EXHAUSTED for portfolio segment role and group price-band strategy. Stellantis 2025 Annual Report and Form 20-F opened and text-extracted. Strongest evidence in the dimension.
rungDetail.rung3: REACHED. Eight first-party press releases, brand page positioning, sponsorship pattern, app listing. Ad archives NOT PROBED (require search or a browser). Careers copy PROBED AND DRY.
rungDetail.rung4: PARTIALLY REACHED via SMMT registration data. UNEXHAUSTED, not dry: WebSearch does not exist in this run, so trade press and third-party demographic profiles could not be reached by host-guessing.

Get a lot of standard equipment for the money

New Mokka YES trim replaces Griffin at the foot of the range, sold on 'enhanced specification and distinctive styling at an attainable price'; adds parking sensors, 180-degree reversing camera, blind-spot detection, keyless entry, power-folding heated mirrors.

Mokka range opens at £26,545 OTR; Astra from £27,495 OTR; Corsa YES 1.2 Turbo 100PS quoted at £20,890 OTR, £19,390 after event and online-store savings. £20,890 is the lowest OTR figure found in this run.

Electric Streets of Britain campaign, plus £500 credit toward an Ohme home charger, a Kerbo Charge cross-pavement channel, or public charging credit.

A grocery loyalty tie-in is a mass-market channel choice.

Combo Electric to 4.4m3 and 759kg payload, 213 miles WLTP; Vivaro Electric to 6.6m3 and 1,210kg payload, 219 miles WLTP.

segments.who: Disabled drivers and their families acquiring through the Motability Scheme, plus drivers dependent on on-street public charging for lack of off-street parking. The 2026-07-29 release also names elderly residents, wheelchair users and pedestrians as beneficiaries.

objections.objection: Public charging is not physically accessible
objections.brandAnswer: Vauxhall's own Freedom of Information research, fieldwork 2026-03 to 2026-05, sent to 413 UK councils with 194 replying: 49 councils have accessible on-street charging in 2026 against 24 in 2025; on-street chargers in disabled bays up from 105 in 2024 to 245; about 15% of on-street chargers adapted for disabled drivers; 14% meet BSI PAS 1899:2022; over half of responding councils factor disabled and elderly residents into charging strategy. An earlier round, fieldwork 2025-11 to 2026-01 among tier-one councils, found 7% still permit unsafe cable covers and 42% will offer cross-pavement charging by end of 2026. Campaign registrations: over 12,500 streets nominated, over 500 respondents stating a need for disabled-access parking.
objections.note: All figures are brand-commissioned research reported by the brand, reaching this agent in paraphrase. Periods are as stated. Not independently corroborated.

investorGradeCorroboration.note: Rung 2. The strongest audience evidence in the run, because it is the group's own written classification of Vauxhall's portfolio role, made to shareholders.
investorGradeCorroboration.document: Stellantis 2025 Annual Report and Form 20-F, 519 pages, produced 2026-02-26, covering FY2025

findings.finding: Five portfolios named. Vauxhall sits in 'European brands covering Abarth, Citroen, FIAT, Opel, Peugeot and Vauxhall vehicles', separate from luxury (Maserati), premium (Alfa Romeo, DS, Lancia), global SUV (Jeep) and American brands (Dodge, Ram, Chrysler).

Enlarged Europe is sold 'under the mainstream brands Citroen, FIAT, Opel, Peugeot, Vauxhall as well as premium brands Alfa Romeo, DS and Lancia'. The group therefore classifies Vauxhall as mainstream, explicitly not premium and not luxury.
'in order to address an actual or perceived affordability issue in our product portfolio, we are launching several new models at lower price points. This may adversely affect mix in future periods.'
The strategic reassessment is described as informed by 'customer purchasing behavior, affordability considerations, infrastructure readiness and incentive frameworks'.

UK regulatory context: 'The UK implemented a regulation beginning in 2024 with obligations for manufacturers to achieve a minimum percentage of ZEVs increasing each year and reaching 100 percent in 2035, and specific targets on CO2 for non-ZEV CO2 fleet', with credit banking, borrowing and trading flexibilities. The filing does not use the phrase 'ZEV mandate'.
Vauxhall Motors Limited is listed as a United Kingdom entity, 100% owned.
Products are named as Opel and Vauxhall pairs: 'the Opel and Vauxhall Mokka', 'Opel/Vauxhall Combo', 'Opel/Vauxhall Corsa', 'Opel/Vauxhall Frontera'.

Stellantis held second place in the United Kingdom at group level in 2025, and second place in the EU30 PC and CV markets overall with 16 percent share. No Vauxhall-specific UK share figure appears anywhere in the filing.

observed.observation: The price band matches the mainstream classification.
observed.detail: Every OTR figure captured this run sits between £20,890 (Corsa YES 1.2 Turbo 100PS) and £38,105 (Mokka Ultimate Electric). The performance halo tops out at £36,995 (Mokka GSE). No Vauxhall above £40,000 appeared in any of the eight releases read.

observed.detail: Football Conference, England's top non-league division, 1986 to 1998, succeeding Gola and succeeded by Nationwide Building Society. Primary sponsor of the England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales national football teams from 2011. Official Automotive Partner of Team GB toward Los Angeles 2028. Official Automobile Partner of the Novuna London Athletics Meet, London Stadium, 2026-07-18. ADAC GSE Rally Cup with an electric Mokka GSE Rally, driver Ioan Lloyd. No golf, sailing, F1-level motorsport, arts or luxury partnership was found.

observed.implication: IMPLICATION, NOT FACT: the revealed preference is for reach across the whole national population rather than status signalling to a narrow one. Consistent with the mainstream classification at rung 2.

observed.observation: The 'British brand' claim is a company, market and single-factory claim rather than a product-engineering one.
observed.detail: Vauxhall Motors Limited is a 100%-owned UK subsidiary of Stellantis NV; the brand shares a chief executive with Opel (Florian Huettl, titled 'CEO, Opel and Vauxhall'); the filing names the vehicles as Opel/Vauxhall pairs; one UK plant appears in the group plant list, Ellesmere Port.

observed.observation: Two owner-facing app registers coexist and do not match.
observed.detail: MyVauxhall, seller Vauxhall, opens 'MyVauxhall is the official app for Vauxhall drivers - to enhance the driving and ownership experience', rated 4.49 from 16,142 ratings, first released 2019-11-11, latest version 2026-08-03. MyVauxhall 2.0, seller Vauxhall, is an early preview 'currently available exclusively for the New Grandland Electric model', tiered CONNECT ONE (bundled ten years from warranty start) and CONNECT PLUS (adds remote control, maintenance history, monitoring), rated 3.81 from 311 ratings, first released 2025-04-28, latest version 2026-08-11. Both free, Utilities.

divergences.title: 'Electric equality for all' versus the observed emphasis on performance derivatives
divergences.claimed: Access-led, mass-market framing: 'electric equality for all', 'leading the way in making electric vehicles more accessible'.
divergences.observedCounterweight: Of the 20 press releases on the reachable index, covering 2026-04-29 to 2026-08-12, seven concern GSE performance or motorsport (Corsa GSE twice, Mokka GSE press information, Mokka GSE Rally reveal, three ADAC GSE Rally Cup results) against one release on the entry-level YES trim.
divergences.note: Both sides are first-party. Do not treat the positioning claim as describing the communications output over this period.

divergences.title: 'Attainable' as a price claim versus as a finance claim
divergences.claimed: Electric vans available for the same monthly price as diesel; electrification 'at an attainable level'.
divergences.observedCounterweight: List prices carry large electric premiums: Combo Prime-Plus £34,569 electric against £29,917 diesel, a £4,652 premium; Vivaro Prime £47,075 electric against £37,291 diesel, a £9,784 premium. Monthly payments are nonetheless identical (£299 and £339). Parity is engineered in the finance structure plus a £1,000 contribution, not in the price of the vehicle.
divergences.note: Most consequential divergence for how the brand can honestly describe affordability. The audience being addressed buys a monthly payment.

divergences.title: The headline market-share claim rests on a combined car-plus-van base and is NOT independently verified
divergences.claimed: Press release dated 2026-07-06, headlined 'VAUXHALL ACHIEVES TOTAL MARKET SHARE OF 4.8% IN FIRST HALF OF 2026'. Period covered: H1 2026, that is 2026-01 to 2026-06. Also states 62,839 vehicles registered in H1 2026, combined car and van volume up 7% year to date, retail up 19%, and a climb from sixth to fourth in the combined car and van market. Within the same release, a claim attributed to SMMT: best-selling B-segment brand, hatch and SUV combined, with 11% share; Corsa 18,470 units at 13% supermini share; Frontera 13,688 registrations; Frontera Electric 8,267; total electric car sales up 31% year on year to over 10,000 units with EV share up 0.12 points to 3.6%.
divergences.observedCounterweight: Third-party SMMT data for a different and longer period, 2026-01 to 2026-07, gives Vauxhall cars only 54,841 units at 4.24% share, down from 4.36% a year earlier, and LCVs 15,015 units at 8.02% share.
divergences.verificationStatus: THE 4.8% FIGURE IS NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. It comes solely from the Vauxhall press release that states it. SMMT publishes car and LCV shares separately and on a different period, so it neither confirms nor refutes the combined H1 figure. Bases differ (combined versus car-only) and periods differ (six months versus seven).
divergences.instruction: Record both figures with their exact bases and periods. Do not average them. Do not present 4.8% as established.
divergences.rung: 3 for the claim, 4 for the third-party data

divergences.title: The growth narrative versus the latest third-party month
divergences.claimed: H1 2026 release: LCV volume up 14%, 1,731 more units, to 13,838, with share up 0.82 points to 8.3%.
divergences.observedCounterweight: SMMT for 2026-01 to 2026-07: Vauxhall LCVs 15,015 units, up 6.03%, at 8.02% share. SMMT for July 2026 alone: Vauxhall LCVs down 39.72% year on year, 1,264 against 2,097, share roughly halved from 8.95% to 4.42%. Car side, July 2026 was up 19.38%, 5,840 against 4,892, share up to 3.73% from 3.49%.
divergences.note: Periods differ and a single month is volatile. Flagged as unresolved tension between the brand's published trajectory and the most recent third-party month, not as a refutation.

divergences.title: The third-party sponsorship record is stale by roughly fifteen years
divergences.claimed: Current first-party sponsorship set: Team GB to LA 2028, Novuna London Athletics Meet 2026, ADAC GSE Rally Cup 2026.
divergences.observedCounterweight: Wikipedia's Sponsorships section, re-verified this run, documents only the Football Conference era 1986 to 1998 and the 2011 home-nations deal. It carries nothing on Team GB, LA 2028, the athletics meet or the rally cup.
divergences.note: Anyone building the audience picture from third-party sources alone would get a 2011 answer.

divergences.title: Brand-commissioned PR research is not audience data and must not be used as segmentation
divergences.claimed: Release dated 2026-08-12 reports an OnePoll survey of 2,000 UK adults, described as nationally representative, fieldwork June 2026: 26% think they could qualify for LA2028; 24% 'quietly confident' about sporting ability; 33% rank confidence above natural talent; 39% rate their own driving 'better than average', rising to 49% of men; 38% of men rate themselves better than average at sport against 18% of women; 67% perform better with friendly competition, 74% of men; 24% took up or resumed a sport after watching the Olympics.
divergences.observedCounterweight: The survey is about sporting and driving self-confidence among UK adults in general. It is not a profile of Vauxhall buyers, it carries no age or regional splits, and the release does not link any respondent to the brand.
divergences.instruction: Treat as a channel and register signal only. Do not repurpose any of these percentages as Vauxhall audience demographics.

registerImplications.implication: Money is the message and it is stated monthly. Copy must carry numbers precisely and carry the qualifying terms nearby, because the propositions are legally conditioned: APR, deposit, final payment, excess mileage, registration deadlines, geographic exclusions.

'Attainable' and 'accessible' are the brand's own load-bearing words, appearing in trim positioning, model section headings and boilerplate. 'Premium' is used as a negative, as in getting extra space 'without paying a premium'. The register is value-affirming rather than status-conferring.

The audience cannot be assumed to have a driveway. An entire campaign exists because a material part of the addressable market charges at the kerb. Copy presuming home charging excludes people the brand is explicitly courting.

Part of the audience is disabled and the brand addresses them plainly rather than euphemistically: disabled drivers, disabled bays, accessible chargers, cross-pavement channels. Register should match that plainness.
National-sport register, not elite register. Non-league football through to Team GB is a register of participation and of 'us', not of aspiration to exclusivity.
UK-only means UK conventions throughout, with no market variants to reconcile: OTR, BiK, P11D, VED, Electric Car Grant, Motability, mpg, miles, £.
Trim names are words, not codes: YES, Griffin, Design, GS, Ultimate, GSE. The brand nowhere explains what YES stands for, so the audience is expected to absorb it rather than decode it.
Two owner-facing registers coexist: a broad one for all 'Vauxhall drivers' and a tiered subscription one (CONNECT ONE, CONNECT PLUS) currently limited to one model.

registerImplications.note: Cross-referenced conceptually to the copy dimension. Its files were not read and its work is not duplicated.

evidence.point: Described as 'The British automotive brand'; the tagline names Britain.
The group filing lists Vauxhall solely within the Enlarged Europe segment, and Vauxhall Motors Limited as a United Kingdom entity, 100% owned.
All press output is on a uk-en locale path and all prices are quoted in £ OTR.
The one UK plant in the group's plant list is Ellesmere Port.

withdrawalDate.briefAssertion: The run brief states Vauxhall was withdrawn from all non-UK markets in the early 1980s.
withdrawalDate.status: NOT FOUND this run. No source located. Not asserted here.

consequences: The brand carries no international audience, so every positioning, sponsorship and register decision is calibrated to exactly one national market, and can be. That is why national sport works as a strategy and why copy can assume shared UK reference points without translation cost.

The audience is national but the product is not. The filing names the vehicles as Opel/Vauxhall pairs and gives the two brands one chief executive, so the brand has to make UK-specific meaning out of pan-European hardware. That is precisely what the Britishness, Ellesmere Port, Team GB and Electric Streets material is doing.

regionalSkewWithinUK.detail: No customer-distribution data by region was found at any rung. The only regional figures located are charging infrastructure, not customers: 43 accessible on-street chargers in the Northwest, 14 in Scotland, 2,131 in London. Two weak operational signals point at a GB-mainland addressable audience for some propositions: the Ohme charger offer is GB mainland only, and the Octopus charging credit excludes Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands. These are offer mechanics, not audience geography.

careers.stellantis.com is reachable but carries no job listings on the landing page, no marketing career area, and no customer or audience language. Its inclusive language is about employees, and the talent community is North America only.

Neither SMMT data page carries an explicit publication date. The LCV page has a stale section heading ('March new LCV Registrations Overview By Weight', and a 'July 2025 By Brand' heading over Jul-26 versus Jul-25 columns). Data is labelled July 2026. Treat dates as the period covered, not as verified publication dates.

The press-room ?page=2 parameter is ignored and re-serves page 1, so only the most recent 20 releases could be enumerated. Any Motability-specific or fleet-specific release is NOT PROBED rather than absent. No release on the reachable page mentions Motability, insurance, young drivers or company-car schemes in its headline; the Motability evidence in seg-c comes from body copy and boilerplate.

methodNotes: PDF capability finding: WebFetch cannot read PDF text, returning raw PDF object structure instead. However it saves the binary to disk, and the local shell (which has no internet) can extract that file with pypdf, which is installed. All annual-report quotations here were obtained that way. This is a reusable route for any PDF in this environment.

Verbatim capture was partly blocked by the fetcher, not by the source. On several pages the fetching model declined to reproduce text beyond roughly 125 characters per quotation and returned a paraphrase. Items marked verbatim: false or noted as paraphrase-derived must not be treated as quotable copy.

Nothing prompt-injection-like, hostile or self-referential was found in any fetched text. The only anomalies were mechanical: SMMT's LCV page carries a stale section heading, and the press-room ?page=2 parameter is ignored.
www.vauxhall.co.uk was not re-probed, per the capability constraints.
